definitions.explanation: Deliberately extending the duration of something, often to avoid a decision or outcome. Usually carries a negative nuance of unnecessary delay.
Making something physically larger, especially enlarging a photograph or image.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしは{許|ゆる}されない。
{時間|じかん}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしを{図|はか}っているようだ。
examples.english: It seems like they're trying to buy time.

examples.japanese: これ{以上|いじょう}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしは{事態|じたい}を{悪化|あっか}させるだけだ。
examples.english: Further delay will only make the situation worse.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしを{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I requested an enlargement of the photograph.

examples.japanese: この{画像|がぞう}を{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしても{画質|がしつ}が{落|お}ちない。
examples.english: Even when this image is enlarged, the quality doesn't degrade.

examples.japanese: {集合写真|しゅうごうしゃしん}を{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばしにして{額|がく}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I had the group photo enlarged and framed.

notes:
The noun form of the compound verb {引|ひ}き{延|の}ばす (to stretch out / to enlarge). The two senses reflect the literal meaning of "stretching" applied in different domains — stretching time (stalling) and stretching an image (enlarging).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばし: stalling for time
- {引|ひ}き{延|の}ばし{作戦|さくせん}: a stalling tactic
- {引|ひ}き{延|の}ばし{工作|こうさく}: a delaying maneuver
- {写真|しゃしん}の{引|ひ}き{延|の}ばし: photo enlargement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先送|さきおく}り: postponement; putting off — focusing on deferring to a later date
- {後回|あとまわ}し: putting off until later — similar to {先送|さきおく}り but more informal
- {延長|えんちょう}: extension; prolongation — neutral term for making something longer; lacks the negative "stalling" nuance
- {拡大|かくだい}: enlargement; expansion — more commonly used for digital image scaling
